newsitem.title: CANADA: Rival bidders galore seen for Morrison.
newsitem.headline: Rival bidders galore seen for Morrison.

text.p: Several Canadian energy companies are viewed as possible rival bidders for Morrison Petroleums Ltd, the target of a C$652 million hostile offer from Canadian 88 Energy Corp.

Analysts said on Monday that as many as seven companies with interests in deep natural gas exploration in southwestern Alberta's foothills could launch competing offers to Canadian 88's cash and stock bid.
Canadian 88 plans to offer C$10 a share, up to C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each share of Morrison, which has virtually no debt after a series of asset sales.
Potential white knights mentioned include Norcen Energy Resources Ltd, Rigel Energy Corp, Shell Canada Ltd, Alberta Energy Co Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc.
Even Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, which currently has a hostile offer in play for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, was viewed as a potential bidder for Morrison.

Norcen, which has been restructured after selling more than C$1 billion of assets over two years, is Morrison's partner in the Racehorse Creek foothills gas play next door to Canadian 88's huge gas discovery made last year at Waterton.
Morrison, whose stock performance has recently lagged its peer group, reported disappointing drilling results at Racehorse Creek late last year.

Shell Canada, though not seen as an aggressive bidder, was also in a good position because of its dominance and expertise in the strategic exploration area, said Scott Inglis, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp.

"They have stated that they're looking for acquisitions in Canada, this is a core area for them and they have the cash to do it. So, from that perspective, you would have to consider them a player," Inglis said.
He said that Alberta Energy favored being placed in a "white knight" situation and was expanding its foothills gas exploration program. "I'd say AEC is a player," he said.
Morrison gained an estimated C$240 million from the formation of a royalty trust on the cash flow from an Alberta gas plant and British Columbia oil pipeline and other recent oil and gas asset sales.
The cash would pay down Morrison's debt to between zero and C$30 million, Inglis said.

"I think 88 is being opportunistic by making a bid when the stock has been out of favor," he said, adding that Morrison's Coleman gas plant in southwestern Alberta was a coveted prize for Canadian 88.
Morrison shares were up 1.60 to 10.10 today on 12.1 million shares, making it by far the most active issue on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Canadian 88 was off 0.25 to 6.50 on 35,199 shares.
